PROJECT 01 · NFA_04 · UNIT STANDARD 114053

System Monitoring, Memory Testing & Backup Planning

Monitoring CPU and memory health, and designing a secure backup plan for a multi-user server environment.

RAM diagnostic test

THE SCENARIO

I had to test the RAM of my computer with a diagnostic tool: first planning the test with a date and time, then running it and keeping the output as evidence so any errors could be justified and rectified, and finally recording the date, time and output in an Excel spreadsheet.

Test plan

  • Date: 24 April 2025
  • Time: 2:00 PM
  • What will be tested: I will be testing RAM(Memory) to see if has any problems.
  • How the test will be conducted: I will use Windows Memory Diagnostic Tool:
  1. On the search tab, search for Windows memory diagnostics. / Type mdsched.exe in Run.
  2. Choose "Restart now and check for problems".
  3. System will restart and run test.

CPU performance monitoring

THE SCENARIO

I had to monitor my CPU performance over time with Windows Performance Monitor, using the %Processor Time and %Idle Time counters and capturing each step. I then compared my results with another student’s and answered follow-up questions on whether the CPU performance was good enough and whether it can be improved.

%Processor Time

%Idle Time

Comparison with another student

My CPU %Processor Time averaged around 25% while my classmate’s averaged 39%. This shows that my system was less busy during the testing period. Also, my idle time was higher than theirs, indicating that my laptop has better CPU availability.

Is the CPU performance good enough for the PC?

Yes. Based on my testing, the CPU performance is good. It handled tasks without delay, and the %Processor Time was not too high during basic operations.

Are there means to increase CPU performance?

Yes. The means to increasing the PU performance could be include: Upgrading the CPU, closing background apps, increasing RAM, and cleaning out malware can all help improve performance(if there’s malware in the device).

PROJECT 02 · NFA_02 · UNIT STANDARD 114047

Windows 11 Pro Deployment Plan

THE SCENARIO

As the IT technician for ITCA, I was tasked with installing Windows 11 Professional on 5 new PCs for staff members. Before touching any machine, I had to produce a deployment plan covering a hardware and software review, milestones and time estimates, minimal disruption to staff, a risk assessment, a backup of the installation for future troubleshooting, and a review procedure to confirm the result matches ITCA's instructions.

Deployment plan

a. Review plan

  • Hardware specs: Confirm CPU, RAM, storage, TPM & UEFI compatibility.
  • Software: Ensure licenses are available (for Windows 10 Pro, drivers, antivirus, Microsoft Office, etc.).
  • Staff usage: take note of what applications and configurations each staff member needs.

b. Milestones and time estimates

MilestoneDeadline
Review hardware/software specs, prepare installation mediaDay1(2-3 hrs per PC)
Install Windows 11 Pro on test machinesDay 3(30 mins per PC)
Backup old dataDay 4(30 mins per PC)
OS installationDay 5(1–2 hrs per PC)
Install drivers & updates and Install software & testDay 6(2–3 hrs per PC)
User acceptance testing & handoverDay 7

c. Minimize disruption to staff

  • Schedule installations during off-hours or low-activity periods.
  • Communicate with staff about potential downtime.
  • Install PCs after office hours or during weekends.
  • Communicate downtime schedule to staff in advance.

d. Risk assessment

RiskMitigation
Hardware incompatibilityCheck compatibility before installation.
installation errorsTest on one PC before rolling out to all 5.
hardware failureVerify installation media before use
Data loss during installationCreate a full data backup before installation Create a full data backup before installation.

e. Backup plan

I didn’t have a USB for the backup image but this is the procedure I would follow:

  • Full user data backup to external HDD or cloud storage.
  • Keep recovery USB drive for Windows 10.
  • Create a system image backup of the Windows 11 Pro installation for troubleshooting

f. Review procedure

The procedure:

  • Confirm Windows 10 Pro is installed and activated.
  • Verify drivers, updates, antivirus.
  • Run sample tasks to confirm apps & peripherals (printer, network, etc.) work.
  • Document results for ITCA approval, including screenshots pf windows 11 Pro installation

Evidence · OS installation, step by step

PROJECT 05 · NFA_15

Windows Server Administration: Domain Controller, Hyper-V, Backup & Printing

Four practical server-administration tasks covering safe domain controller operations, role installation with PowerShell, backup and printer deployment.

Domain controller start-up & shut-down

THE SCENARIO

I had to show the exact steps to start up a Domain Controller from a powered-off state and to shut one down from a running state, keeping the business’s staff in mind. Any problems appearing during the procedures had to be addressed, or the absence of problems documented.

a) Start-up from power off

  • Press the Power button on the server or VM hosting the Domain Controller.
  • Wait for the operating system (Windows Server) to boot up completely.
  • Log in with an Administrator account to confirm the Domain Controller is online and services (like AD DS and DNS) are running.

b) Shut-down from a running state

  • Log in with an Administrator account on the Domain Controller.
  • Go to Start - Power - Shut down, or use the command: shutdown /s /t 0
  • Wait for the server to safely power off, ensuring all AD services stop properly.

c) Addressing problems

During the start-up and shut-down process, no problems were detected. If issues had occurred (e.g., boot errors, replication problems, or unresponsive services), I would have checked the Event Viewer logs and ensured the Domain Controller was reachable on the network.

Installing Hyper-V with PowerShell

THE SCENARIO

Using PowerShell, I had to install the Hyper-V role on a Windows Server, then identify a way to automate that installation across a group of servers.

Steps

  • Open PowerShell as Administrator.
  • Run the following command: Install-WindowsFeature Hyper-V -IncludeManagementTools -Restart
  • Allow the server to restart automatically to complete installation.

Automating across multiple servers

The solution was to use PowerShell Remoting with a script to run the same command on multiple servers.

Script I used: Install-WindowsFeature Hyper-V -IncludeManagementTools -Restart

Backing up a shared folder with Windows Server Backup

THE SCENARIO

I had to back up a shared folder to a shared network location using Windows Server Backup, then restore that backup to an alternate location with the same utility to prove the backup was not corrupt.

Installing and sharing a printer

THE SCENARIO

I had to install a printer and share it on the local network.

a) Install and share the printer

I installed the printer by going to Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners and adding my printer. Once installed, I opened Printer properties → Sharing tab and selected Share this printer. This allowed the printer to be available to other users on the same network.

PROJECT 06 · NFA_11

Securing Desktops & Servers: Policy, Backup and Access Control

THE SCENARIO

As the network administrator at ITCA, I carried out a set of security tasks: reviewing the organisation’s security policy, securing desktop computers against malware and illegal software, protecting server data with backups and restricted permissions, identifying logon problems, applying security improvements, and resolving an access problem for the Backup Operators group.

Security policy

Poster location

The Security Policy poster will be placed in visible areas where all staff can see it. These will include the reception area, the staff kitchen, board room, and in class rooms where lecturers are always working.

Proof staff have read and understood the policy

All staff members will attend a short security awareness session and will be required to sign an acknowledgement form confirming they have read and understood the policy.

Securing the desktop computers

Scan for malware

A malware scan was performed using Windows Security. There were no found threats but if found then they would have been removed.

Identify illegal software

The desktop computer was checked under “Installed app” for unlicensed or illegal software. Any unauthorized software was removed.

Steps I took:

  1. Opened Settings by pressing Win + I.
  2. Navigated to Apps → Installed apps.
  3. Looked through the list for any suspicious or unlicensed programs, such as Cracked Office.
  4. Selected the unlicensed software and clicked Uninstall.
  5. Followed the prompts to complete the removal.
  6. Restarted the computer to make sure the program was fully removed

Record findings

No illegal software or malware was found.

Securing the server computers

Create a backup

A backup of the “SharedData” folder was created using Windows Backup and stored on the network location \\ServerBackup\2025\.

The backup was done in using “Backup and Restore(windows 7)”

Restore the backup

The backup was successfully restored to an alternate location (windows SSD:\RestoreTest) to verify that the backup was not corrupt.

Configure backup folder permissions

Permissions were configured so that only the Administrators group has full access to the backup location.

Managing server security

Identify logon issues

Logon issues were identified using the Event Viewer under Security Logs. Event Viewer was also used to review security logs including logon attempts, privilege use, and file access events.

Security improvements

Security improvements I applied include:

  • Enabling Account Lockout Policy after 3 failed login attempts.
  • Applying Windows Updates to keep systems secure.

Technical support

Why Backup Operators cannot connect

The Backup Operators group could not connect to the backup folder because permissions were restricted to Administrators only.

Solution

The Backup Operators group was added to the folder permissions with Modify and Read access. This allows them to access backups with minimal administrative effort.
